in_sanskrit.name: सविता
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: Savitri, the Goddess of the Sun, is the wife of Surya, the Sun God. She is also known as Savitri Devi, Savitri Mata, or simply Savitha. In Hindu mythology, Savitri is revered for her devotion, wisdom, and strength. She is believed to protect her family, especially her husband, and is often invoked for success in various endeavors.

in_hindi.name: सविथा
in_hindi.long_meaning: Savitha in Hindi is a derivative of the Sanskrit word सविता (Savitā), meaning 'Goddess of the Sun'. The Hindi name सूर्यवती (Sūryavatī) is also used interchangeably to mean 'Goddess of the Sun'. Savitha or Sūryavatī is revered for her devotion, wisdom, and strength, and is believed to protect her family and provide success in various endeavors.

in_tamil.name: சவிதா
in_tamil.long_meaning: In Tamil, the name Savitha (சவிதா) is derived from the Sanskrit word सविता (Savitā), meaning 'Goddess of the Sun'. The Tamil name அத்தியால் ஸூர்ய அமிகவேலை (Attiyāl Sūrya Amigavēlai) is also used to refer to the Goddess of the Sun. Savitha is revered for her devotion, wisdom, and strength, and is believed to protect her family and provide success in various endeavors.

Savitha is mentioned in various Vedic texts, including the Rigveda and the Mahabharata, and is revered as the wife of Surya, the Sun God. She is also known for her devotion, wisdom, and strength, and is believed to protect her family and provide success in various endeavors.
